title: Florida Compliant Drivers Program: What It Really Is, and the Discounts Florida Drivers Can Actually Get
description: No Florida agency runs a 'compliant drivers program'. Here is what those ads really are, and the real state-approved discounts that lower Florida car insurance.
author: Insurance Bhaiya Research Desk
keyTakeaways: No Florida state agency operates a 'Compliant Drivers Program'. The phrase is used in online ads and lead-generation sites, not by the FLHSMV or the Office of Insurance Regulation.
Being 'compliant' in Florida simply means carrying $10,000 PIP and $10,000 Property Damage Liability continuously; there is no bonus rate for it.
The state-approved discount route is the mature driver course for drivers 55 and older, authorized under Florida Statutes section 627.0652, with a discount that typically lasts three years.
Real savings also come from safe-driver rating, telematics, bundling and choosing the right deductible, all of which are offered by licensed insurers, not by 'programs'.
If a landing page asks for your Social Security number or driver's license number to 'check program eligibility', close it.

faqs.question: Is the Florida Compliant Drivers Program legit?
faqs.answer: It is not a government program. The name is used by private marketing and lead-generation sites. You can still get a legitimate quote through them, but the price comes from a regular insurer, and your contact details are usually shared with multiple agents.

faqs.question: How do I get the Florida mature driver insurance discount?
faqs.answer: If you are 55 or older, complete an FLHSMV-approved mature driver course and send the completion certificate to your insurer. The discount typically lasts three years if you avoid at-fault crashes and moving violations; the amount is set by your insurer.

faqs.question: What insurance do I need to be legal in Florida?
faqs.answer: $10,000 Personal Injury Protection and $10,000 Property Damage Liability, held continuously for the whole registration period. Drivers with certain violations must also file an SR-22 or FR-44; see [SR-22 vs FR-44](/qa/sr22-vs-fr44-difference). For how this compares with other states, read our [state auto insurance compliance guide](/learn/state-auto-insurance-compliance-guide).

faqs.question: Why am I getting calls after filling out an insurance quote form?
faqs.answer: Many quote sites are lead generators that sell your details to several agents or call centers. Check the consent text near the submit button. You can ask each caller to place you on their internal do-not-call list.

content.text: The ad usually looks official: a Florida flag, a headline like 'Florida drivers with no DUIs now qualify for the Compliant Drivers Program', and a button that says 'Check Eligibility'. Thousands of Florida drivers search for the program every month. The honest answer is short. There is no state-run program by that name. This guide explains what you are actually clicking on, and where the real, verifiable savings for Florida drivers come from. For the full picture of what Florida and California require, start with our hub on [state auto insurance compliance](/learn/state-auto-insurance-compliance-guide).
So What Is the 'Compliant Drivers Program'?

Neither the Florida Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles (FLHSMV) nor the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation lists a program with that name. The phrase appears on independent websites and in social media ads that funnel visitors into a quote form. Once you submit it, your details are typically sold to one or more insurance agents or call centers, which is why people who fill these forms often report a burst of calls and texts within minutes.

That is not automatically illegal. Comparison and lead sites are a normal part of insurance shopping. The problem is the framing: an ad that implies government backing, an exclusive rate, or a deadline to 'claim' a benefit is selling urgency, not a discount. Any price you end up with still comes from an ordinary insurer using its ordinary filed rates.

content.title: Regulators Are Watching This Exact Tactic
content.text: In 2025 the Federal Trade Commission reached a $45 million settlement with lead generator MediaAlpha over health insurance ads that faked an affiliation with the government and then fed consumer data to aggressive telemarketers. The auto version of the playbook works the same way. A genuine government program will be on a .gov site and will never ask for your Social Security number to show you a 'rate'.
Compliance in Florida is a legal minimum, not a discount tier. Every vehicle with four or more wheels registered in Florida must carry:

items: **$10,000 Personal Injury Protection (PIP)**, which pays 80% of necessary medical expenses for you and certain passengers regardless of fault, up to the limit. Its 14-day treatment rule catches many people out; see [Florida PIP insurance explained](/learn/florida-pip-insurance-explained).
**$10,000 Property Damage Liability (PDL)**, which pays for damage you cause to other people's property.

**Continuous coverage for the whole registration period**, even if the vehicle is parked. A lapse can suspend your license and plate for up to three years, with a reinstatement fee of up to $500. The fee steps are in [what happens if car insurance lapses in Florida](/qa/what-happens-if-car-insurance-lapses-in-florida), and the complete list is in [Florida minimum car insurance requirements](/qa/florida-minimum-car-insurance-requirements).

content.text: Notice what is missing: bodily injury liability. Most Florida drivers are not required to carry it, which means a 'compliant' policy can leave you personally exposed if you injure someone. Bodily injury liability becomes mandatory only after certain violations, through an SR-22 or, for DUI, an FR-44 filing at 100/300/50. If you are facing one of those, read [SR-22 vs FR-44: what is the difference](/qa/sr22-vs-fr44-difference).

content.title: Compliant Is Not the Same as Protected
content.text: A Florida minimum policy has no bodily injury coverage and only $10,000 for property damage. Hit a newer SUV and the repair bill alone can exceed your limit, with the difference coming from your savings. Read [can a car insurance company sue you](/qa/can-a-car-insurance-company-sue-you) to see how insurers recover what they pay out.
The Real Discounts Available to Florida Drivers

rows: State-approved course providers; discount applied by your insurer

Authorized by Fla. Stat. 627.0652. Discount typically lasts 3 years if you avoid at-fault crashes and moving violations. Amount set by each insurer. How to claim it: [Florida mature driver insurance discount](/learn/florida-mature-driver-insurance-discount).
Drivers with an eligible noncriminal moving violation
Electing the course can keep points off your record, which protects your rate. Limited number of elections allowed.
Drivers with clean records for the insurer's look-back period
This is the legitimate version of what the ads describe; it is built into normal quotes.
Drivers willing to share driving data via app or device
Savings depend on braking, speed, phone use and mileage. Poor scores can raise rates with some insurers.
Bundling with home, renters or RV coverage is often the single largest discount.

content.text: Your deductible is the other lever you control. Raising a collision [deductible](/glossary/deductible) lowers the premium, but only makes sense if you could pay that amount from savings tomorrow. Run the numbers in the [Deductible Breakeven Calculator](/deductible-calculator/) before you change it.
How to Tell a Real Quote From a Lead Form

items: **Check who is quoting.** A real quote names a licensed insurer or agency. You can verify an agent's license through the Florida Department of Financial Services.
**Look at the URL.** State programs live on .gov domains. 'Program' sites on .com domains are private businesses.
**Watch the data request.** Your name, ZIP code and vehicle are enough for a ballpark quote. A request for your Social Security number before any price is shown is a red flag.

**Read the fine print.** Lead sites usually disclose, near the submit button, that you consent to be contacted by 'marketing partners'. That sentence tells you the site is selling your contact details.
**Ignore deadlines.** Insurance rates are filed with the state. There is no expiring 'enrollment window' for a safe-driver price.

content.text: Florida vs California: Different Rules, Same Lesson

California drivers see similar ads, but California does have a genuine state program for income-eligible drivers, the California Low Cost Auto Insurance Program, and stricter proof rules. If you split time between the two states or are moving west, compare the obligations in our [California evidence of liability insurance](/learn/california-evidence-of-liability-insurance) guide. Snowbirds who travel by motorhome should also read [California RV insurance](/learn/california-rv-insurance), because a Florida-registered RV still has to satisfy liability rules on California roads, and a full-timer setup changes what coverage you need.

And if the move west includes buying a house with a small down payment, the lender will add its own insurance requirement on top of your auto policy; see [California private mortgage insurance](/learn/california-private-mortgage-insurance) for how that bill works and when it ends.
